- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.4) — reduce forecast peak heights.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward spikes (sentiment < 0.2) — adjust downward bias to avoid “rebound overcorrection.”
- Lagged price movements often overshoot — dampen forecast slope after recent sharp moves.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., 0.5 → 0.1) triggers downward correction — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — smooth 3-day moving average before applying sentiment-weighted adjustments.
